edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 11

source_text: Similis est fratruelis meus capreae hinnuloque cervorum in montibus Bethel. Haec duo animalia in scripturis saepius nominantur, et quo magis admiranda sunt, eo magis Dominum significant. Caprea acutissime videt; hinnulus cervorum saltu celeri montes transit. Christus et acute videt occultorum et saltu celeri de caelo in terras descendit et de terris ad caelum ascendit. Montes Bethel — Bethel interpretatur domus Dei — prophetas et apostolos intellege, in quibus habitat Deus.
pass_a_gloss: Like is my brother to-gazelle and to-young-of stags on mountains of-Bethel. These two animals in scriptures rather-often are-named, and by-how-much more they-are to-be-wondered, by-that-much more the-Lord they-signify. Gazelle most-sharply sees; young-of stags by-leap swift mountains crosses. Christ both sharply sees hidden-things and by-leap swift from heaven onto lands descended and from lands to heaven ascended. Mountains of-Bethel — Bethel is-interpreted house of-God — prophets and apostles understand, in whom dwells God.
pass_b_english: [[My brother is like a gazelle and like a young stag on the mountains of Bethel >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:9]]. These two animals are named rather often in the Scriptures, and the more they are to be wondered at, the more they signify the Lord. The gazelle sees most sharply; the young stag crosses the mountains with a swift leap. Christ both sees hidden things sharply and, with a swift leap, came down from heaven to earth and ascended from earth to heaven. The mountains of Bethel — Bethel is interpreted house of God — understand as the prophets and apostles, in whom God dwells.
